  C. RESOLUTION NO. 22-69 AMENDING THE AUTHORIZED SCHEDULE OF
  COMPENSATION & BENEFITS FOR REGULAR NON-REPRESENTED
  EMPLOYEES AND INCREASING GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS FOR
  REGULAR NON-REPRESENTED EMPLOYEE SALARIES AND BENEFITS

  Over the last few months, staff has met with the Focus Group to discuss the
  status of the Authorized Schedule of Compensation and Benefits (ASCB) for the
  City’s regular non-represented employees and presented its recommendations
  for updating the ASCB for Fiscal Year (FY) 2022-23. Resolution No. 22-69
  amends the ASCB for all regular non-represented employees, effective July 2,
  2022. The amended ASCB for the City’s regular non-represented employees is
  expected to have an annualized cost impact of $382,133.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-69, which
  amends and approves the ASCB for the City’s regular non-represented
  employees for the period covering July 1, 2022, through June 30, 2023, and
  increases General Fund appropriations $307,261 and various other special
  funds $74,872 to cover increased costs to salaries and benefits for the City’s
  regular non-represented employees.

  D. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH ARCHITERRA DESIGN
  GROUP FOR LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTURAL PROFESSIONAL SERVICES

  On August 16, 2022, the City of San Gabriel issued a Request for Proposals (RFP
  22-07) for a qualified firm to provide landscape design and plan check
  professional services. The City received three proposals and in staff’s opinion
  Architerra Design Group best met the criteria outlined in the RFP. The Fiscal
  Year 2022-23 budget includes $12,500 for landscape architectural services as
  an estimate of the services needed. If additional funds are needed due to
  activity in the City, the funds will be transferred, or additional appropriations
  will be requested. The additional activity will result in additional revenue.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Professional Services
  Agreement with Architerra Design Group and authorize the City Manager to
  execute said agreement and issue a purchase order.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 1, 2022  3
   E. SELECTIVE TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM (STEP) GRANT

  The Police Department has received a renewed grant from the Office of Traffic
  Safety (OTS) to participate in the Selective Traffic Enforcement Program (STEP)
  for Federal Fiscal Year 2022-2023. The grant will reimburse the City for
  personnel overtime costs incurred in participating in this campaign and the
  purchase of related equipment for training in the sum of $85,000. City Council’s
  approval of the resolution would authorize acceptance of the Grant Funding
  and amend the current budget approving the allocation of funds not to exceed
  the amount of $85,000 to be reimbursed by OTS based on actual funds used
  during the federal fiscal year grant (10-01-2022 through 09-30-2023).

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-65 approving
  and accepting the OTS contact funding outlined in the staff report and increase
  the Revenue Budget Account 147-3229 by an estimated $85,000 to reflect
  receipt of the grant funds and increase Police Department Expenditure Budget
  by $85,000, in various accounts of fund 147, the OTS fund, which will be used
  for overtime costs and the purchase of any related equipment.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. ORDINANCE NO. 686 – ADOPTION OF 2022 CALIFORNIA BUILDING AND
  FIRE CODES

  The California Building Standards Commission has adopted new building & fire
  codes to take effect on January 1, 2023. Publications were available as of July
  this year. The Building & Safety Division and Fire Department staff have
  monitored and participated in the development of these codes closely and are
  engaging in training to ensure that the City’s building and safety and fire
  personnel are properly trained to implement the new standards. Implementing
  and enforcing the most current building codes will result in safter buildings and
  communities that suffer less damage when natural disasters occur. There is no
  fiscal impact related to this item.

  B. DISCUSSION REGARDING UNIVERSAL SHOPPING PLAZA

  At the October 4, 2022, City Council meeting, business owners and tenants of
  the shopping center known as Universal Shopping Plaza (140 West Valley
  Boulevard) provided public comments regarding the pending exterior
  improvement project at the site. Many of the tenants expressed frustration over
  the project and the uncertainty with their tenancy at the shopping center.
  Subsequent to public comment, the Council directed staff to agendize a report
  to the Council regarding the matter. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the matter, allow for additional
  public comments, and then receive and file the report.

MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 1, 2022

I  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Ding called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:35
  P.M. on Tuesday, November 1, 2022, in the San Gabriel Mission Playhouse, 320 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Ding .

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Denise Menchaca, Carina Rivera, John Wu, Vice Mayor
  John R. Harrington, and Mayor Tony Ding .
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith

I  Lemieux, Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk
  Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg
  de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Finance Director William Kaholokula, and Community
  Development Director Aldo Cervantes.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Ding announced that the agenda order was approved .
  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. INTRODUCTION AND PROMOTION OF FIRE CAPTAIN PHILIP APPARIS

I  Fire Chief Wallace made the presentation and Chief City Clerk Clark administered
  the Oath of Allegiance.

  B. NATIVE AMERICAN HERITAGE MONTH

  Mayor Ding made the presentation and Chief Anthony Morales, Gabrielino Band
  of Mission Indians, accepted the proclamation.

  C. LUNG CANCER AWARENESS MONTH

  CITY COUNC IL REGULAR MEETING M INUTES  Page 1 of 6  November 1, 2022
   Mayor Ding made the presentation.

  D. UNITED AGAINST HATE WEEK - ASIAN YOUTH CENTER/LA VS. HATE

  Mayor Ding made the presentation and Asian Youth Center Stop Hate Program
  Manager Heidi Lau accepted the proclamation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

I  Debbie Kilgore, resident, commented on illegally-placed election signs; suggested
  campaign-spending limits; and commented on alleged unethical campaigning.

  Jan Phan, resident, commented on alleged unethical campaigning .

  Sue Fitzsimmons, resident, commended the San Gabriel Police Department's
  Community Engagement Team for their recent creative problem-solving to help a
  resident.

  San Gabriel Police Chief Harris reminded the community to be aware of pedestrians
  with the upcoming time change and hours of darkness, encouraged pedestrians to
  wear reflective clothing, and announced that reflective bracelets and vests are
  available free from the Police Department's Traffic Bureau .

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Chief City Clerk Clark announced that pursuant to Government Code §54953(c)(3)
  reporting requirements, Consent Calendar Item C included changes in salary and

I  benefits for all unrepresented employees, including executive management, as
  follows: a 3% salary increase; an increase from 8 to 16 floating holiday hours; an
  increase in the uniform allowance from $800 to $1000, effective calendar year 2023;
  and an increase of one full day bereavement pay for employees who must travel more
  than 200 miles. In addition, new hires starting January 1, 2023, shall be excluded from
  receiving retiree medical benefits pursuant to Resolution No. 03-27, and shall instead
  receive the Public Employees' Medical Hospital Care Act statutory minimum as set
  forth in Government Code §22892 upon their retirement from the City.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Rivera, to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4E as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  MENCHACA, RIVERA, WU, HARRINGTON, DING
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

I  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the following :

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of October 18, 2022.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of October 18, 2022.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 6  November 1, 2022
   The City Council approved October 6, 2022, and October 13, 2022, Registers of
  Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. RESOLUTION NO. 22-69 AMENDING THE AUTHORIZED SCHEDULE OF
  COMPENSATION  & BENEFITS FOR REGULAR NON-REPRESENTED
  EMPLOYEES AND INCREASING GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS FOR
  REGULAR NON-REPRESENTED EMPLOYEE SALARIES AND BENEFITS

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 22-69, which amends and approves the

I  ASCB for the City's regular non-represented employees for the period covering July
  1, 2022, through June 30, 2023, and increases General Fund appropriations
  $307,261 and various other special funds $74,872 to cover increased costs to
  salaries and benefits for the City's regular non-represented employees.

  D. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH ARCHITERRA DESIGN GROUP
  FOR LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTURAL PROFESSIONAL SERVICES

  The City Council approved the Professional Services Agreement with Architerra
  Design Group and authorized the City Manager to execute said agreement and
  issue a purchase order.

  E. SELECTIVE TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM (STEP) GRANT

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 22-65 approving and accepting the OTS
  contact funding outlined in the staff report and increasing the Revenue Budget
  Account 147-3229 by an estimated $85,000 to reflect receipt of the grant funds
  and increasing Police Department Expenditure Budget by $85,000, in various

I  accounts of fund 147, the OTS fund, which will be used for overtime costs and the
  purchase of any related equipment.

  Clarifying discussion included that applications in process before January 1, 2023,

  There was no public comment.

  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  RECESS AND RECONVENE

I  The meeting was recessed at 7:21 P.M. and resumed at 7:30 P.M. with all Council Members
  present.

  B. DISCUSSION REGARDING UNIVERSAL SHOPPING PLAZA

  Community Development Director Cervantes made the presentation. A certified
  translator provided translation in Cantonese and Mandarin as requested.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 6  November 1, 2022
   City Attorney Lemieux clarified that the decision of the Design Review Commission
  would not be reviewed as part of this item; it was a discussion item only.

  The following tenants of the Universal Shopping Plaza (Focus Plaza) shared their
  negative experiences with the landlord's management staff in regard to lack of
  notice, stalling tactics for lease renewals, huge rent increases if they stay, and about
  their potential losses from investment in their stores if their lease is not renewed
  or if the stores must close for an extended period: Dave Barela, JD & Associates;
  Bin Hong, Business Owner; Ke Wong, resident; Jimmy Ha, resident and tenant;

I  Vivien Chen, tenant; Dennis Leung, tenant; Andy Kuai; Grace Cheung, tenant;
  Jessica, resident and tenant; Min Xiang, tenant; and Yan Ha Liu, tenant.

  RECESS AND RECONVENE

  The meeting was recessed at 8:48 P.M. and reconvened at 8:56 P.M. with all Council
  Members present.

  Discussion included the City's relocation assistance for the tenants; whether
  tenants would be reimbursed by the landlord for the improvements they have
  made; the landlord's indication that they might help fund tenant relocation; the
  landlord had been invited to attend the Council meeting; the landlord is doing the
  improvements to help compete with facilities like the Santa Anita mall; notification
  process for the Planning Commission meeting and possible reasons tenants didn't
  receive notice; possibility for the project to be completed in two phases and
  challenges of staying open during renovations; the City's notification requirements;
  Council desire for future notification to be multilingual; Council desire to
  investigate what happened to the notices and why only one person showed up to

I
  the Planning Commission meeting; the tenants' effort to obtain legal help; fiscal
  impact to the City in lost revenue and jobs for forced vacancies; the project only
  required Design Review Committee action in terms of architecture and design, the
  project was identified under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) as
  being exempt from environmental requirements; relocation challenges; definitions
  of finishes versus structural changes; Council desires to have a staff report if
  anything in an application indicates tenants are being evicted; possibility of a new
  hearing if the scope requires it; and a Code update to have the application include
  whether a project would require evictions.

  There was a consensus of the City Council to direct the City Manager and City
  Attorney to propose a solution to the City Council before the end of the year.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Isela Bowles expressed disappointment that business owners needed to attend the
  meeting for the previous item; commended Vice Mayor Harrington for being the voice
  for the businesses in the City, and expressed dissatisfaction with a disconnect between
  the City Council, Commissioners, and businesses.

I  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT - None.

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Menchaca invited all to the City's Dia de los Muertos event on
  November 3, 2022, from 6:00 - 9:00 P.M. at the Mission Playhouse.

  Mayor Ding thanked the Community Services Department for the Fall Fun Festival, and
  reported on a round table discussion with Assemblymember Mike Fong and California

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 5 of 6  November 1, 2022
